subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this generated-versus-external MCPorter classification and per-agent daemon ownership as the permanent compatibility contract for existing QMD users?
rationale: The implementation can be reviewed mechanically, but deciding when OpenClaw owns a generated configuration versus defers to user configuration changes upgrade behavior, daemon lifecycle, credential boundaries, and failure handling for existing installations.

options.title: Adopt after corrections
options.body: Fix the discovery-order documentation, refresh the branch and live upgrade proof, then merge the per-agent ownership contract.

options.title: Narrow to environment isolation
options.body: Land only the proven XDG process-environment separation and defer generated configurations and per-agent daemon ownership to a smaller follow-up design.

options.title: Keep current ownership
options.body: Decline generated per-agent MCPorter configuration and retain user-managed MCPorter configuration and daemon behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt after corrections
recommendation.body: Fix the discovery-order documentation, refresh the branch and live upgrade proof, then merge the per-agent ownership contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail most directly connects this person to the original MCPorter-backed QMD integration and daemon contract.
